doc.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Ten years since the last interview: Connecticut and Hartford
summary: Jackson sums up the decade: moved to Connecticut and chairs the Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz at the University of Hartford.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive. I’m happy to have Javon Jackson remotely with me today. It’s been almost ten years since we last had an interview when you were at Hamilton College, and can you sum up those ten years?

Well time goes fast, first thing. Since then a lot has occurred. I’m now living in Connecticut, I’m the chair of the Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz at the University of Hartford. So now I live in the State of Connecticut, where at that time I was living in New Jersey. So things are going good. I’ve had a lot of great opportunities that have been afforded to me and still enjoy a performance career, although performing right now is on a hiatus for many of us, all of us. So with that, the ten years have been good.
